The competition was organised by the [[French Football Federation]] (FFF) and is open to all clubs in [[Football in France|French football]], as well as clubs from the [[Overseas France|overseas departments and territories]] ([[Guadeloupe]], [[French Guiana]], [[Martinique]], [[Mayotte]], [[New Caledonia]], [[French Polynesia|Tahiti]], [[Réunion]], [[Collectivity of Saint Martin|Saint Martin]], and [[Saint Pierre and Miquelon]]). The defending champions [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]], who beat [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] 5–1 in the [[2023 Coupe de France final|previous year's final]] to claim their first Coupe de France title,{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65439267|title=Nantes 1 Toulouse 5 |date=29 April 2023|work=BBC Sport|access-date=11 May 2023}} were eliminated in the round of 32 by third-tier [[FC Rouen]]. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] defeated [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] 2–1 in the [[2024 Coupe de France final|final]] for a record-extending fifteenth Coupe de France title.{{cite news|url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/Other-Competitions/2024/05/25/coupe-de-france-final-dembele-powers-psg|title=Coupe de France Final: Dembélé powers PSG|date=25 May 2024|website=Ligue 1|access-date=25 May 2024}} ==Dates== Dates for the first two qualifying rounds, and any preliminaries required, were set by the individual Regional leagues.
